<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Mathmitch7" />{{rh|Wiſedomes praiſe.|Prouerbes.|Dauids care.}}</noinclude>{{Verse|3|3}} Let not mercy and trueth forſake thee: *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Exod. 13.9 duet.6.8.}} bind them about thy necke, write them vpon the table of thine heart.

{{verse|3|4}} *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Pſal. 111.10.}} So ſhalt thou find fauour, and ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, good ſucceſſe.''}} good vnderſtanding in the fight of God, and man.

{{verse|3|5}} ¶ Truſt in the {{sc|Lord}} with all thine heart; and leane not vnto thine owne vnderſtanding.

{{verse|3|6}} *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* 1. Chron. 28.9.}} In all thy wayes acknowledge him, and he ſhall direct thy pathes.

{{verse|3|7}} ¶ *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Rom. 12.16.}} Be not wiſe in thine owne eyes: feare the {{sc|Lord}}, and depart from euill.

{{verse|3|8}} It ſhalbe †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Hebr. medicine.''}} health to thy nauill, and †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Hebr. watring, or moyſtning.''}} marrow to thy bones.

{{verse|3|9}} *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Exod. 23.19. and 34.36. deut. 26.2. &c. mala. 3.10. &c. luke 14.13.}} Honour the {{sc|Lord}} with thy ſubſtance, and with the firſt fruits of all thine increaſe.

{{verse|3|10}} *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Deut. 28.8.}} So ſhall thy barnes be filled with plenty, and thy preſſes ſhall burſt out with new wine.

{{verse|3|11}} ¶ *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Iob 5.17. hebr. 12.5. apoc. 3.19.}} My ſonne, deſpiſe not the chaſtening of the {{sc|Lord}}: neither be weary of this correction.

{{verse|3|12}} For whom the {{sc|Lord}} loueth, he correcteth, euen as a father the ſonne, {{smaller|in whom}} he delighteth.

{{verse|3|13}} ¶ Happy {{smaller|is}} the man {{smaller|that}} findeth wiſedome, and †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Hebr. the man that draweth out vnderſtanding.''}} the man {{smaller|that}} getteth vnderſtanding.

{{verse|3|14}} *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Iob 28.15. &c. pſal. 19.10. pro.8.verſ.11. and 19. and 16.16.}} For the merchandiſe of it {{smaller|is}} better than the merchandiſe of ſiluer, and the gaine thereof, then fine gold.

{{verse|3|15}} She is more precious than Rubies: and all the things thou canſt deſire, are not to be compared vnto her.

{{verse|3|16}} Length of dayes {{smaller|is}} in her right hand: and in her left hand, riches and honour.

{{verse|3|17}} Her wayes {{smaller|are}} wayes of pleſantneſſe: and all her pathes {{smaller|are}} peace.

{{verse|3|18}} She {{smaller|is}} a tree of life, to them that lay hold vpon her: {{smaller|and}} happy {{smaller|is}} euery one that retaineth her.

{{verse|3|19}} The {{sc|Lord}} by wiſdome hath founded the earth; by vnderſtanding hath he ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, prepared''}} eſtabliſhed the heauens.

{{verse|3|20}} By his knowledge the depthes are broken vp; and the cloudes droppe downe the dew.

{{verse|3|21}} ¶ My ſonne, let not {{smaller|them}} depart from thine eyes: keepe ſound wiſdome and diſcretion.

{{verse|3|22}} So ſhall they bee life vnto thy ſoule, and grace to thy necke.

{{verse|3|23}} *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Pſal. 27.24. and 91.11.}} Then ſhalt thou walke in thy way ſafely, ⁊ thy foot ſhall not ſtumble.

{{verse|3|24}} When thou lyeſt downe, thou <!--2nd col-->ſhalt not be afraide: yea, thou ſhalt lye downe, and thy ſleepe ſhalbe ſweet.<noinclude></noinclude>
